transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Well, I guess I’m here because things have just gotten really out of hand lately. After I eat way too much, I keep going into the bathroom and making myself throw up. I just can't stand the idea of gaining weight, you know? It’s stressful. 

Kind of like work lately, actually. I’m a mechanic down at the auto shop on 4th, and man, we've been completely slammed. Just yesterday I had this guy bring in an '08 Honda Civic, complaining about this loud rattling noise, and I swear to you he had about fifty empty soda cans just rolling around in the back seat. I told him, buddy, I think I found your rattle. I mean, people are just wild with how they treat their cars, they never do the preventative maintenance and then they act shocked when the transmission slips. 

But anyway... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. The bathroom stuff. Yeah, I just... I'm terrified because it's gotten to the point where I'm scared I actually can't stop doing it anymore.
Can you tell me more about your concerns with gaining weight? For example, how much does the fear of gaining weight influence what or how much you eat?

Well, it influences everything, honestly. I mean, even if I just see a single pound up on the bathroom scale, I start to completely panic. It makes me feel like all that time I spent laid up with my bad back a couple years ago is finally catching up to me and turning me soft. I'll start planning how to undo it before I can even think straight, you know? 

Speaking of that bad back, man, that was a nightmare. I pulled it trying to lift a transmission out of a Ford F-150. You wouldn't believe how heavy those things are, and my buddy Dave was supposed to be spotting me, but he was distracted on his phone. Probably texting his ex-wife again. They have this whole dramatic on-again, off-again thing that just exhausts everyone in the shop. We keep telling him to just block her number, but he never listens. It's like he enjoys the misery or something. He came in last week with a black eye and tried to tell us he walked into a door, but we all knew it was her new boyfriend. 

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the weight thing. Yeah, so if the scale moves even a tiny bit, I just freak out and have to fix it immediately.
How often do you find yourself going to the bathroom and making yourself throw up after eating?

Well, it's pretty often, honestly. For at least the past three months, there's hardly been a single week where I didn't have one of those huge late-night eating episodes and then, you know, go make myself throw up right after. Some weeks it happens several times. It's usually worse when I'm stuck at home more because my back is acting up again. 

Which, by the way, it has been killing me this week. I think it's because I was working on this vintage Mustang on Tuesday—beautiful car, cherry red, original interior—but the guy had let it sit in a damp garage for like ten years, so everything underneath was rusted solid. I spent three hours just trying to torque off a single exhaust bolt. My boss, Greg, he's this old-school guy who thinks WD-40 fixes everything, he just kept yelling at me to put some elbow grease into it. I told him, Greg, my elbow grease is fine, but my lumbar spine is screaming. He doesn't get it, he hasn't actually touched a wrench since the 90s. He just sits in the office playing solitaire on his computer and drinking that awful decaf coffee. I don't even know why people drink decaf, it's like, what's the point? 

But yeah, anyway... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? I got sidetracked. Oh, right, how often I do it. Yeah, so, almost every week for the last three months, sometimes a few times a week. It's just... a lot.
You mentioned that after eating too much, you go to the bathroom and make yourself throw up. Can you tell me exactly how often that happens, like how many times a week or month?

Well, I think I just said, it's pretty much every week for the last three months, sometimes a few times a week. It really just depends on how stressed I am or if I'm stuck at home. Being stuck at home is the worst, honestly. I get so restless. 

I actually tried taking up knitting to keep my hands busy when I'm just sitting around. My sister-in-law, Brenda, she knits these incredible sweaters, like the kind you'd pay a hundred bucks for at a boutique. She tried to teach me, but my hands are so calloused from the shop that the yarn just keeps catching on my skin. It's so frustrating. Plus, Brenda is one of those people who is just naturally good at everything, you know? She bakes, she gardens, she probably speaks French or something. It's annoying. We went to her house for Thanksgiving last year and she had made everything from scratch, even the cranberry sauce. Who does that? I usually just buy the canned stuff. I actually like the shape of the can ridges on the jelly, it's nostalgic. 

But, uh, anyway... yeah, I already told you, it's almost every week, sometimes more.
Can you give me a more specific average — how many times per week would you say you make yourself throw up after eating?

I mean, if I had to put a number on it... I'd say maybe three or four times a week? Sometimes more, like maybe five or six if things are really bad. It's just, like I said, for the past three months, it's been pretty much every single week. I have those big eating episodes late at night, and then I just have to get rid of it. It definitely spikes when my back is acting up and I'm stuck on the couch. 

Being on the couch just makes me think about how much I hate our living room furniture. We bought this sectional from one of those big box discount stores, and I swear the cushions started sagging after like two months. My husband, Tom, he refuses to replace it because he says it's "broken in" now. But it's not broken in, it's just cheap foam. He falls asleep on it every night watching those historical documentaries. The ones about World War II. I don't know how he can watch that stuff right before bed, it's so depressing. All that black and white footage of tanks and people looking miserable. I'd rather watch a cooking show, though I guess that doesn't help with the whole eating thing, does it? 

But yeah, anyway... what did you ask? A specific average? Yeah, probably around three to five times a week, give or take.
Besides making yourself throw up, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight?

No, I don't really do any of that stuff. Just the throwing up. I tried going for a run once, like, years ago, but my knees just can't take it. And honestly, who has the energy for that after working all day? 

Speaking of energy, I've been trying to get Tom to take these new vitamins I bought. They're supposed to be, like, all-natural, whole-food sourced or whatever. The lady at the health food store—she had this crazy long gray hair, like down to her waist, and she was wearing Birkenstocks with socks, which is just a choice, you know?—anyway, she swore by them. Said they'd give him a boost. But he just leaves the bottle sitting on the kitchen counter. It's right next to the toaster, which is also broken, by the way. The lever won't stay down unless you jam a butter knife in there, which I'm pretty sure is a fire hazard. I told Tom to fix it, but he just says we should eat less toast. He's so stubborn. Like, it's a toaster, Tom, not a complicated engine rebuild. I could probably fix it myself if I brought my tools inside, but I try to leave work at work, you know? 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, laxatives and stuff. Yeah, no, I don't use any of those. Just the throwing up.
Do you ever restrict your food intake, fast, or follow strict diets to control your weight?

No, I don't really do the whole fasting or strict diet thing. I don't know how people even stick to those. A couple of the guys at the shop, Dave and Marcus, they tried doing that Keto thing last year. Have you heard of that? They were basically just eating blocks of cheese and bacon for lunch every single day. The breakroom smelled like a grease trap for a month. 

And Marcus, he’s our transmission guy, he got so cranky without carbs that he actually threw a wrench across the garage and dented the fender of this pristine '68 Mustang we had in for a rebuild. The boss was absolutely furious. It took us three days to pound that out and color-match the paint, which is a total nightmare on those vintage models because the original paint fades in this really specific way, you know? You can't just slap a factory code on it and call it a day, you have to blend it perfectly or it looks like a cheap patch job. I actually really love doing the paint matching, it's kind of like an art form. It takes a good eye. My dad taught me how to do it when I was a teenager, back when he had his old Chevy... 

But, uh, wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, restricting food and diets. No, I don't do any of that. I just eat a lot, and then, you know, do the other thing.
